summary: IFR lets trained pilots fly without visual reference. Outside take-off and landing, stay 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km (2,000 ft over high or mountainous terrain). Above 3,000 ft amsl or the transition altitude, cruise at semicircular levels: magnetic track 000° to 179° odd thousands, 180° to 359° even thousands (VFR adds 500 ft). In controlled airspace an IFR flight needs a flight plan and clearance, and reports position as callsign, position, time, level, next position and estimate.
sections: Instrument Flight Rules (SERA.5015)
VFR is too restrictive for regular air services, so properly trained pilots with suitable instruments can fly in cloud and other non-visual conditions under the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).
Only two flight categories exist: VFR or IFR.
The minimum height rule
Except for take-off or landing, or when specifically authorised, an IFR flight must not fly below the minimum flight altitude set by the State overflown. Where none is set:
– over high terrain or mountainous areas: at least 2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the aircraft's estimated position
– elsewhere: at least 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km
Exam trap The distance is 8 km of the aircraft's position, not 600 m (that is the congested-area low-flying rule) and not nautical miles.
Cruising levels: the semicircular rule (SERA.5015, Appendix 3)
In level flight above 3,000 ft amsl, or above the transition altitude if that is higher, choose a cruising level by the semicircular rule. Flight levels use 1013.2 hPa.
The level depends on magnetic track:
– 000° to 179° (east): IFR at odd thousands (FL30, 50, 70, 90 ...); VFR at odd thousands plus 500 ft (FL35, 55, 75 ...)
– 180° to 359° (west): IFR at even thousands (FL20, 40, 60, 80 ...); VFR at even thousands plus 500 ft (FL45, 65, 85 ...)
Above FL290 the steps change (FL300, 310 ... with 1,000 ft RVSM spacing up to FL410).
An IFR aircraft may cruise at another level when ATC instructs it or in a notified holding procedure.
Memory aid East is odd ("Every Odd Day"), west is even.
Flight plan and ATC clearance (SERA.5020)
Before any IFR flight in controlled airspace, the commander must file a flight plan (whether IMC or VMC) and get an ATC clearance based on it.
In controlled airspace an IFR pilot must follow:
– the ATC clearance and any further instructions
– the published holding and approach procedures at the destination, unless ATC says otherwise
You may cancel IFR and continue VFR if you can stay in VMC while in controlled airspace and you tell ATC, asking them to cancel your IFR flight plan.
If you have to depart from these rules to avoid immediate danger, tell ATC as soon as possible.
Unless the flight plan has been cancelled, tell ATC when you land within or leave controlled airspace.
Position reports (SERA.5025)
An IFR flight in, or about to enter, controlled airspace reports time, position and level at notified reporting points or intervals, or when ATC asks.
Order: aircraft callsign, position, time, level, next position and estimate.
Example: "G-ABCD, Wicken four seven, flight level four zero, Marlow five seven".

sum.Instrument Flight Rules (SERA.5015): IFR is for flight without visual reference; every flight is either VFR or IFR.
sum.The minimum height rule: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km, or 2,000 ft over high or mountainous terrain.
sum.Cruising levels: the semicircular rule (: Track 000° to 179°: odd thousands; 180° to 359°: even thousands. VFR adds 500 ft.

cards.a: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the aircraft.

cards.q: IFR minimum height over high or mountainous terrain?
cards.a: 2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km.

cards.q: When does the semicircular rule apply?
cards.a: In level flight above 3,000 ft amsl or the transition altitude, whichever is higher.

cards.q: What two things must an IFR flight have in controlled airspace?
cards.a: A filed flight plan and an ATC clearance.

cards.q: Can an IFR flight switch to VFR in CAS?
cards.a: Yes, if it can stay in VMC and tells ATC to cancel its IFR flight plan.

cards.q: Order of an IFR position report?
cards.a: Callsign, position, time, level, next position and estimate.

cards.q: Is the semicircular rule based on true or magnetic track?

quiz.q: The minimum height for IFR flight over non-mountainous terrain is:
o: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the aircraft
1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m
1,500 ft above the highest obstacle within 10 nm
1,000 ft above ground level
quiz.why: SERA.5015: 1,000 ft within 8 km (2,000 ft over high terrain). The 600 m figure belongs to the congested-area low-flying rule.

quiz.q: Over mountainous terrain an IFR flight must be at least:
o: 2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km
2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 nm
1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km
1,500 ft above the highest obstacle within 5 km
quiz.why: Mountainous areas double the margin to 2,000 ft; the radius stays 8 km.

quiz.q: An IFR flight on a magnetic track of 175° should cruise at:
o: FL70
FL80
FL75
FL60
quiz.why: 000° to 179° takes odd thousands, so FL70. FL75 would be a VFR level; FL80 and FL60 are for westbound tracks.

quiz.q: A VFR flight on a magnetic track of 260° following the semicircular rule would choose:
o: FL65
FL55
FL60
FL70
quiz.why: 180° to 359° is even thousands; VFR adds 500 ft, giving FL45, 65, 85. FL60 is the IFR level.

quiz.q: Above which level does the semicircular rule apply in level flight?
o: 3,000 ft amsl or the transition altitude, whichever is higher
3,000 ft amsl or the transition altitude, whichever is lower
FL100
The transition level
quiz.why: The higher of 3,000 ft amsl and the transition altitude.

quiz.q: Before an IFR flight in controlled airspace in VMC, the commander must:
o: File a flight plan and obtain an ATC clearance based on it
Obtain an ATC clearance; a flight plan is needed only in IMC
File a flight plan; no clearance is needed in VMC
Book out with the departure aerodrome only
quiz.why: SERA.5020: flight plan and clearance, whether IMC or VMC.

quiz.q: The correct order for an IFR position report is:
o: Callsign, position, time, level, next position and estimate
Callsign, position, level, next position and estimate
Ground station, position, time, level, next position and estimate
Callsign, position, time, next position, level and estimate
quiz.why: Time comes after position and level after time. Leaving out the time, or starting with the ground station, is the trap.

quiz.q: An IFR flight in controlled airspace in VMC wishes to continue VFR. It must:
o: Stay in VMC and tell ATC, asking them to cancel its IFR flight plan
Leave controlled airspace first
Simply change its squawk to 7000
Get a Special VFR clearance
quiz.why: Cancelling IFR is allowed if you can stay in VMC and tell ATC.
